capabilities: Pseudonymize terms manually via right-click rules or via local NER entity detection
Import transcripts from noScribe, SRT, CHAT/CLAN, Markdown and plain text
Manage correspondence rules at file, folder and vault scope with exceptions and priorities
Export pseudonymized versions, correspondence tables and re-export as VTT/SRT/CHAT
Organize corpus folders into classes with mirrored transcription, mapping and export folders
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. NER requires a one-time download of ~19 MB WASM plus ~66 MB model, then works offline. All transcript processing is local; only the optional Coulmont first-name lookup contacts an external site. v0.1.x with active roadmap phases; citation info (APA, BibTeX) is provided for academic use.
intentEvidence: existing tools (Sonal, Whispurge) do not integrate into a note-taking and analysis environment
motivation: The author built it to fill the gap of pseudonymizing interactional transcripts for linguistics and conversation analysis research directly inside a note-taking vault.
problem: Existing pseudonymization tools do not integrate into a note-taking environment, and Obsidian has no built-in way to anonymize qualitative research transcripts.

relations.evidence: Sonal pi — Following a meeting with Maxime Beligné
Queries coulmont.com — suggests sociologically equivalent first names
Install the Data Files Editor plugin to view mapping JSON files directly
Xenova — ONNX model conversion and transformers.js library, enabling local execution

requires.name: coulmont.com web service (optional, only for equivalent first-name suggestions)

summary: Transcript pseudonymization tool that replaces identifying names, places and institutions in research transcripts with tracked pseudonyms and export-safe correspondence rules.
